title: Frozen Eleum Loyce
snippet: At some point Alsanna reached Eleum Loyce and became close to the Ivory King. She was in truth a fragment of the Dark Soul of Manus, Father of the Abyss, that, despite the fact that he had been killed centuries in the past, had retained some of his will and power. Alsanna was born as the incarnation of Manus' fears and despite being a frightened and frail thing she managed to to coalesce once again absorbing the other humanities, and then obtain the shape of a human, with her own self-awareness. To sustain herself and seek more power, she sought the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strenght. Alsanna thus sought the Ivory King to sustain herself and smother her innate fear and was accepted by him, quietly finding a place at the side of the leader of Eleum Loyce where he provided her comfort and she accepted Eleum Loyce as her home.

title: Alsanna, Silent Oracle
snippet:
Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna. Upon his departure, he gifted her an intertwined blade of shadow and light, revealing to her that he had already known about her Dark nature. He traveled deep into the Chaos for one final assault but was eventually devoured by its flames. In a last ditch attempt to quell the fiery Chaos, the Gates of Eleum Loyce were opened, allowing the cold harsh blizzard to consume the kingdom whole.

In spite of all this, Alsanna bravely chose to remain and devoted herself to prayer to appease the raging flame in memory of her loving lord. All the while hoping that despite all odds, he might perhaps one day return.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet:
At an unknown point, an ancient Chaos was discovered deep below the land. Legend holds that the Ivory King used his magnificent soul to build Eleum Loyce and contain the spread of Chaos. A grand cathedral was built in an attempt to appease the raging flame, but the Chaos would not be sated. As a precaution, various knights and golems were posted throughout the Garrison Ward to lead the advance on the swollen flame on his orders. Other knights were ordered to delve into the depths of Chaos to exterminate the terrible things that dwelt there, but not one of the knights returned.

Eventually, the Ivory King sensed the degradation of his soul and left Eleum Loyce without a word, leaving everything to Alsanna. He traveled deep into the Chaos until he and his knights were corrupted by the flames. At some point after the King's departure, the ivory gates of the city were flung open, and the land grew cold and lifeless.

Over time he was drained of his vigour and when he sensed the degradation of his power he decided to plunge into Chaos' heart in an attempt to reduce its flames alone. He decided to leave without a word to his subjects and left everything to Alsanna who had now found her place at his side, conferring a sword inscribed with the name of the land to her.  lore : Eleum Loyce is a land far to the north of Drangleic with vast natural deposits of ivory ore. At some point in the distant past, a fragment of the Bed of Chaos, the source of the Flame of Chaos and seedbed of the Demons, survived from Lordran and drifted to settle underground in the region. It started to give birth to atrocities and monsters that cursed the region, leading people to flee in fear.

Not long after, following the collapse of Forossa, the highest ranking knight of its army abandoned his home and reached Eleum Loyce. The proud knight saw the suffering of the population and decided to devote himself to the protection of that great land. And so he took his crown as the new leader of the country and started to fight the raging Chaos thanks to his powerful soul as their Ivory King.

The Old Chaos -  Dark Souls II - location - overview 
 overview : The Old Chaos is a large platform afloat on a sea of lava with roots hanging down from above. Alsanna, Silent Oracle opens the passage to it. After passing through a fog gate, the player drops down a deep pit which deposits them onto the platform. At least one Knight of Eleum Loyce will accompany the player into the Chaos.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Finally, the Bearer of the Curse travels to Frozen Eleum Loyce, once ruled by the Ivory King. Built to contain the Old Chaos, the city was abandoned and froze over when its king vanished into the chaos. Guided by the last child of the Abyss, Alsanna, Silent Oracle, the Bearer of the Curse seeks out the remaining knights of Eleum Loyce to gain their help in braving the Old Chaos. Finding the Burnt Ivory King there, the Bearer of the Curse defeats him and claims his crown.

Once the Bearer of the Curse has found all three crowns of old, along with Vendrick's own crown, the fallen king will unleash the hidden power of the crowns, making the Bearer of the Curse immune to the hollowing effects of the curse. Bidding the Bearer to seek strength, and asking them whether allowing the flames to fade is truly their only choice, the king sends the Bearer of the Curse on their way.

title: Flame of Chaos
snippet:
Flame of Chaos -  Dark Souls - storyline - lore 
 lore : The Flame of Chaos was created by the Witch of Izalith when she attempted to use her Lord Soul to recreate the First Flame. When she was unable to control it, she was consumed by it and transformed into the Bed of Chaos, mother of all Demons. Most of her children were similarly consumed and transformed into monstrosities; her daughter Quelana, however, escaped and used the Flame of Chaos to create the art of Pyromancy.

After the defeat of the Bed of Chaos at the hand of the Chosen Undead, the flames of Chaos persisted. It would eventually be discovered beneath Eleum Loyce, in the form of The Old Chaos. The Old Chaos would go on to consume many of Eleum Loyce's knights, turning them into Charred Loyce Knights, and eventually claiming the ruler of Eleum Loyce himself. The Ivory King would eventually be freed, at the bequest of his oracle Alsanna, by the Bearer of the Curse.

snippet: The highest ranking knight of Forossa, together with Forossan sages and knights, abandoned his home and moved to the northeast of Drangleic before reaching a land that was plagued by a fragment of the Bed of Chaos. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. In shorter terms, the Loyce Souls start dropping much more regularly after the Charred Knights dropping a specific number of items.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Bed of Chaos -  Dark Souls - boss - lead 
 lead : The **Bed of Chaos** (混沌の苗床) is a boss in *Dark Souls*. A hideous lifeform which the Witch of Izalith has turned into, it is found in what remains of her land, Lost Izalith. It is a "puzzle boss" with unconventional mechanics.

Although the traditional way of reaching the Bed involves slaying both the Demon Firesage and the Centipede Demon, a shortcut can be opened by offering Quelaag's Sister 30 Humanity through the Chaos Servant covenant.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Another common strategy is to summon one or two phantoms and position both next to each orb, with the host out of reach of the Bed of Chaos' arm sweeps, but in a direct line towards the entrance to the core. After both phantoms break the orbs, the host can then head to the entrance of its mouth and kill the boss.
A simple solo strategy involves "corpse-running" to the fog door and then running to each orb and then to the Bed of Chaos itself. Some players prefer to stay hollowed so that humanity is not wasted, since many deaths may follow after the first orb breaks.
Players with a high number of Humanities or souls may be interested in investing in some Rings of Sacrifice.
The chaos scythe/fire pick(s) attacks will almost always miss unless the player stays in one spot for too long.
Its bug-like core is immune to fire damage.
It is possible to make the Bed of Chaos's arm push the player towards the branch that leads to the core.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
The greatest concerns to the player over the encounter will be dealing with the boss' broad, sweeping attacks and the large, bottomless holes that open in different parts of the arena.
Once both roots have been cut, the player must reach the boss' heart to access and kill the Chaos Bug, however it is important to be aware that directly in front of the boss is a large bottomless hole. The primary way across is a wide branch that runs from the boss toward where the encounter begins, just below the height of the floor.
A relatively safe method of dealing with both attacks and holes is to hug the walls around the outside of the arena, on the ledges behind the holes and out of reach of the boss (though, not the Volcanic Chaos attack, see below). From here, the player may sprint and jump to cross the holes and reach the orbs if their weight is low enough, or attack the branches and roots from range with magic or a bow.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Bed of Chaos -  Dark Souls - boss - strategy 
 strategy : Unlike most boss encounters, the goal here is not to whittle away the boss's health, but to strike at three vulnerable nodes. Thus, the difficulty in defeating this boss mostly lies in discovering the points to strike while avoiding being knocked in a hole rather than in defeating the boss via conventional methods.
The vulnerable nodes are two roots within glowing spheres, visible to the right and left of the boss at the start of the encounter, and the Chaos Bug within this boss' heart. Striking the roots expands the boss' list of available attacks and 'unlocks' access to the boss' heart.
It is also noteworthy that progress made in damaging one or both of the roots does not reset upon the player's death, allowing repeated attempts at the boss to add incremental progress to the encounter.

title: Bed of Chaos
snippet:
Its bug-like core is immune to fire damage.
It is possible to make the Bed of Chaos's arm push the player towards the branch that leads to the core.
Magic Shield and Strong Magic Shield can be extremely useful against Bed of Chaos, as they can easily block both the scythe and swiping attack with a medium shield without breaking player's guard. This creates a relatively long opening and player can use the remaining stamina to quickly run towards the heart/orb and deal the fatal blow. Lingering Dragoncrest Ring is recommended to counter the short duration of both spells.
One last potential strategy involves the use of shields with high stability. By two-handing a shield such as Havel's Greatshield, and with sufficient Stamina, a player can become almost completely immune to both the damage and knockback effects of the Bed of Chaos's sweeping attacks.

snippet:
Burnt Ivory King -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : **Sword Buff**: Periodically throughout the fight, the King will take a few seconds to buff his sword with magic. Unlike the Smelter Demon, he does not have enhanced defenses during this period, which offers the chance to attack him with impunity.

**Ice Explosion**: Only used when the King has buffed his sword. He will slam the point into the ground, emitting a series of highly-damaging ice spikes in a circle around himself. Easily avoided by moving back from the King when he turns his sword upside down.

**Impale**: Only used with the buffed sword. Similar to Sir Alonne's impale attack, the King will charge up for a moment before lunging at the player. If he connects, he will lift the player on his sword, draining a large amount of health, after which he'll throw the player away.

title: Chaos (upgrade path)
snippet:
Chaos (upgrade path) -  Dark Souls - mechanic - general_information 
 general_information : The Chaos path adds Fire Damage to a weapon, but removes all stat scaling bonuses. This makes it a good choice for lower levels. However, Chaos cannot be augmented. This, along with the lack of stat scaling, ultimately means that Chaos weapons have an inferior damage potential in the long run.

Uniquely for weapon upgrade paths, the Chaos path scales with humanity (up to 10). At 10 humanity, Chaos weapons are superior to Fire weapons (and, indeed, nearly all the other weapon paths in terms of raw damage) that are upgraded to the same level. However, they are inferior if the player is lacking in liquid humanity.

Compared with Lightning weapons, Chaos weapons with optimal humanity deal more damage against unprotected foes; however, as most enemies possess more Flame than Lightning Defense, Lightning weapons are often a better choice.

 usage : If this spell hits directly, it causes great damage; excluding the lava pool produced by Great Chaos Fire Orb, this spell is the most powerful direct-damage pyromancy in the game. While both Great Chaos Fire Orb and Seething Chaos can deal more damage under optimal circumstances, enemies can move away from the lava pool left by Great Chaos Fire Orb, and Seething Chaos requires manipulation and timing in order to deal the most damage.

Unlike its predecessor, Chaos Bed Vestiges does not leave a lava pool, has less range and will begin to arc after a shorter distance (approximately slightly longer than Fire Orb). However, it is easier to reach enemies at higher elevations with this spell than it is with the various "fireball" spells. As well, like its predecessor, its extremely short cast time and fast travel speed allows players to use this spell to quickly punish enemies' openings.

**The unique two-handed strong attack for the Chaos Blade is identical to the two-handed strong attack for the katana weapon class from *Demon's Souls*.
During development, the Chaos Blade was going to be part of a side story involving Shiva of the East, but was cut from the final game. The scrapped story arc was based on one in *Demon's Souls*, in which Satsuki would ask the player to search for the Magic Sword "Makoto", and then attack the player with it upon obtaining the weapon.
The Chaos Blade, and its other variants, is the only occurrence of "Chaos" in the entire series that doesn't deal fire damage.
The Chaos Blade resembles a *[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tachi tachi]*, which has a longer and more curved blade than a standard katana.

title: Chaos Blade
snippet:
The Chaos Blade has the potential for the highest physical damage of the Katanas, with easily the highest Physical damage per second with 10 Humanity and 40 Dexterity at around 450 damage per hit. Do not confuse this with this sword being capable of dealing the most damage of any Katana overall. It causes more Bleed build up than other katanas (36 compared to the default 33 of other katanas). It also has the highest durability of any Katanas, having 50% more than both the Uchigatana and Iaito and twice the amount of the Washing Pole. Like most boss weapons, the Chaos Blade cannot be enchanted by spells or consumables, which lowers its overall damage potential.

In practice, the Chaos Blade is arguably the best Katana for players who don't mind the feedback damage and do not have access to weapon buffs as long as the player can keep up with the requirement of 10 held Humanity to keep full damage, if not Uchi or Iaito would be a better choice.

Chaos Blade (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Much like its original counterpart, the Chaos Blade drains health from its wielder with every successful hit. However, it deals very high damage with each swing, making it a popular choice for PvP or against tougher enemies. The two-handed strong attacks, if they connect, can inflict devastating amounts of damage in the blink of an eye, especially if the weapon is buffed with either resins or spells. It also possesses the highest durability of any katana, though still below average when compared to other weapon classes.

The high damage, along with its ability to be infused and augmented, means that the Chaos Blade can be used for almost any build, providing the high Dexterity requirement and self-damage are not too off-putting.

The Chaos Blade has the highest counter strength of all available katanas, on par with the Lances.

title: Chaos Blade (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
The effect of the weapon can be somewhat offset through the use of passive healing sources, such as the Ring of the Evil Eye, Ring of Restoration or the Replenishment miracle.
Infusing the Chaos Blade with an elemental type (Fire, Magic, Lightning, or Dark) will split the damage evenly, meaning both the physical attack and the attack of the element chosen will be equal to each other. This can be both positive and negative, as the lower physical damage will result in enemies sustaining less damage if they are resistant to the element of choice. However, buffing the weapon with a spell that complements the secondary damage type (i.e. using Sunlight Blade on a Lightning Chaos Blade) will result in a much more formidable weapon for the duration of the effect.
Hitting an opponent while they are invulnerable, such as when rolling or interacting with certain objects, will still activate the self-damage.

snippet: However, the Chaos Blade damages the wielder for slightly more than 1% of their maximum health every time they hit an opponent. This damage can kill the wielder and is not affected by the wielder's defenses or the damage dealt to the target, and will occur even if the target did not take damage from the strike, such as if they blocked or rolled through it. In longer fights, the extra damage taken on top of the opponent's own damage can result in otherwise avoidable deaths if the wielder doesn't manage their health carefully. Equipment such as the Ring of the Evil Eye, Sun Princess Ring, or an off-hand weapon infused with a Blessed Gem, can help with off-setting this damage. Additionally, the weapon cannot be buffed or infused in any way, meaning some specialized builds will be able to gain more benefit from using other katanas.

 benefits : Attain the Great Chaos Fireball pyromancy upon joining. After reaching rank +2, players also attain the Chaos Storm (an upgraded version of Firestorm)
Access to the shortcut to Lost Izalith (the shortcut can be found to the right, before the Demon Firesage boss in the Demon Ruins). The shortcut is one of two ways to save Solaire of Astora.
To open the shortcut door, 30 Humanity must be given **only one time per character**. The Fair Lady must be alive for the door to open.
Players may also reach rank +2 in the covenant and leave, then rejoin to open the shortcut door. Holding the Chaos Storm pyromancy while being in the covenant with the Fair Lady alive appears to be the "key" to this door regardless of current rank.

snippet:

 how_to_join : After defeating Chaos Witch Quelaag, reach the circular room beneath the Bell of Awakening where there are cobwebs lining eggs on the sides. The wall to the right is illusory. Inside, there will be an egg-infected man named Eingyi. The player must answer "Yes" to his question in order for him to move. If the player has answered "No", quitting and reloading will prompt Eingyi to pose his question again. The player may also kill him and join without repercussion. However, this will cost the player his services. Talking to Quelaag's Sister will give the option to join the covenant.

title: Chaos Set
snippet:
Chaos Set -  Dark Souls II - armor - characteristics 
 characteristics : The Chaos Set is one of the most balanced sets in the game. It boasts exceptional fire and dark defenses, as well as good physical defenses for its very low weight, and high magic, lightning, and petrification resistance, as well as poison, bleed, and curse resistance. Its only downsides are that its physical defense will not be enough to protect the wearer from hard-hitting raw physical attacks, so dodging is an absolute must, and it lacks any poise.

Its hood increases casting speed by 5% and the wearer's INT stat by 3 points. The player therefore needs only 13 Intelligence instead of 16 to wear the hood (and the rest of the set) effectively.
